analysis.title: GS TWIG Notes: This Week in Global Research - November 20, 2026
key_insights: GS 2027 US Outlook forecasts above-consensus GDP growth of 2.4% Q4/Q4. Drivers are fading inflation, strong business investment, a resilient consumer and a low-hire, low-fire labor market.
GS expects two more 25bp Fed hikes, in December and March, then gradual rate cuts starting November 2027.
GS Global Rates Outlook (Will Marshall): high starting yields, fading hawkish risks and improved hedge value of bonds should support government bond total returns.

GS US Equity Outlook (Ben Snider) forecasts an 18% total return for the S&P 500, from 18% EPS growth and a stable 18x P/E. The key watch item is 2028 and beyond, as investors question the sustainability of the AI trade.
GS positioning for US equities: hyperscalers, FCF-rich companies returning cash to shareholders, structural growth, and defensive diversification.
GS Global Credit Outlook (Amanda Lynam): higher rates, elevated volatility and a peaking AI growth impulse make the credit cycle increasingly mature. GS expects suboptimal returns.
GS Asia Views (Andrew Tilton): decelerating AI growth meets a fading energy crisis, leaving still-above-trend growth for most Asian economies.
GS Japan Economic Outlook: strong real wage growth and resilient corporate capex offset headwinds from higher interest rates and accelerating inflation.
GS Asia Strategy forecasts a 19% MXAPJ return. It raises China H and India to Overweight and cuts Taiwan and China A to Market Weight to balance AI hardware exposure.
GS China Strategy (Kinger Lau) forecasts 23% upside for MSCI China, driven by accelerating EPS growth and cycle-low valuations, and moves H-shares back to Overweight.
GS Japan Strategy (Bruce Kirk) expects broadening sector performance as government initiatives drive corporate restructuring, M&A and consolidation.
GS EM outlook seeks countries with improving economies. GS upgrades Mexico to Overweight.

GS Euro Area Outlook (Jari Stehn) forecasts 2027 growth of 0.9%, below potential and consensus. High energy prices, tighter credit and French stagnation offset German fiscal expansion and Southern European outperformance.
GS UK Outlook (James Moberly) forecasts above-consensus 1.4% Q4/Q4 GDP growth in 2027.

GS GOAL cross-asset allocation (Christian Mueller-Glissmann) is modestly pro-risk for 2027. On a 12-month view it is Overweight equities and 10-year government bonds, Underweight credit, Neutral commodities.
GS Precious Analyst (Lina Thomas) is constructive on gold in its 2027 outlook.

The US Commerce Department's interim final rule on remote access to advanced semiconductors shifts control from physical GPU exports to access to compute. China's AI labs are most exposed. Large integrated Chinese internet companies (BABA, Tencent, ByteDance) are less exposed.
GS expects China's domestic AI chip market to grow at a 102% CAGR over 2025-30E to US$678bn by 2030E.

GS (Jim Schneider) expects 75% NVDA revenue growth in CY27 from AI demand and buybacks. Risks are new export restrictions, less data center construction after the Blue Wave, and a leadership transition.
GS (Carly Davenport) sees Texas load growth even if data center construction is delayed. Favored IPPs: TLN, VST, NRG.
GS (Alex Blostein) expects re-accelerating management fee growth at alternative asset managers in 2027. Favored: TPG (on conviction list), APO, STEP, CG.
GS hardware bus tour: neocloud bifurcation is increasing, AI infrastructure is becoming more heterogeneous, open and network-intensive, and scale-up Ethernet could be the next networking opportunity.
GS SuperCompute trip: strong demand for 800V power, cooling and liquid cooling, with possible policy headwinds after the midterms. Favored: NVT, ETN, VRT, JCI (on CL), FLEX, APH (on CL).
GS RE+ solar takeaways: residential solar remains subdued while utility-scale solar and storage stay resilient. Favored: NXT (on CL).
GS China shipbuilding trip: demand expected to stay robust through the early 2030s, with strong pricing. Government conservatism and component shortages limit yard capacity expansion.
GS (Michele Della Vigna) expects further acceleration of the LNG investment cycle. Favored: GTT. SBM Offshore initiated at Buy on the deepwater capex wave.
GS healthcare: in China favor Mindray, SNIBE and AngelAlign. In Europe favor AZN, Bayer, ARGX (on CL), GALD, UCB and Sandoz.
GS downgrades Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) to Sell and maintains Buy on ASUR and OMA.
GS upgrades Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, Whitbread and UNFI to Buy.
